beats.care: If you ride a bike, check which pump you use. Ten litres a month at a private pump now costs about fifty rupees more.
beats.what: Nayara Energy and Jio-bp raised petrol by five rupees and diesel by three rupees a litre this month at over 9,000 pumps.
beats.why: Crude oil is above 100 dollars a barrel because of the US–Iran conflict. Private firms can pass on costs; state-run ones haven't.

calc.label: extra a month at Nayara or Jio-bp pumps
calc.q: Litres of petrol you buy a month?

cards.body: Nayara's hike came on 3 October across 7,108 pumps; Jio-bp's on 11 October across 2,304. Commercial LPG also rose ₹62.50 per 19-kg cylinder in October, while home LPG stayed the same.
Indian Oil, BPCL and HPCL have kept pump prices flat. ICRA estimated they lose about ₹8 a litre on petrol and ₹9 on diesel, around ₹530 crore a day together.
cards.title: why don't state pumps raise prices?

cards.body: Nayara raised prices in March too, then cut them in July when crude eased. Private prices can fall as fast as they rise.

cards.q: Should state pumps raise prices too?

opts: Private firms passed on costly crude; state firms absorbed it
Crude got cheaper for state firms only
cards.q: Why are petrol prices different at private and state pumps?
cards.why: Both pay the same high crude price, but state-run firms chose to take losses instead of raising pump prices.

hook: Same petrol, *₹5 more* a litre. Which pump are you filling at?

learn.t: State-run oil companies lost about ₹8 a litre on petrol in September by not raising prices, ICRA estimated.
